kakekotoba.reading_primary: will not exist (I shall not be alive)
kakekotoba.interaction: Not a true kakekotoba pivot itself, but the negative existential sets up the poem's entire premise — 'I shall soon be no more.' Checked against standard pivot canon (なが/よ/あき/まつ/ふる/うき/かる) — none of these sound-pairs appear as double-readings in this poem; あらざらむ, この世, 思ひ出, 今ひとたび, 逢ふ are all single-meaning in context. The apparent candidate 'よ' in 'この世' functions purely as 世 (this world/life) without a second 夜 (night) reading being grammatically active here, since there is no night imagery or context to activate it — so it is excluded as kakekotoba.

bipartite.kami_theme: The speaker, facing imminent death, contemplates having a single memory to carry beyond this world — 'since I shall soon not exist, as a memento for beyond this life'
bipartite.shimo_theme: A desperate wish for one more meeting with the beloved before death
bipartite.pivot_note: The kami-no-ku establishes the mortal condition (impending death, the boundary of 'this world') as the reason/cause for the urgent wish expressed in the shimo-no-ku; the anticipation of death directly motivates and justifies the plea for 'one more meeting,' making the two halves a single unbroken causal utterance rather than a contrastive or metaphorical pairing.

kigo.note: No conventional seasonal image is present in this poem. Every lexical item was checked: あらざらむ (existential, non-seasonal), この世の外 (metaphysical boundary of life/death, non-seasonal), 思ひ出 (memory, non-seasonal), 今ひとたび (temporal but not seasonal), 逢ふ (meeting, non-seasonal). There are no flowers, leaves, birds, insects, dew, frost, snow, rain, moon, wind, mist, grasses, rivers, clothing, or famous places referenced. The poem's imagery is entirely existential/metaphysical (life, death, the afterlife) rather than tied to a season, so season is correctly 'none' despite the requirement to name a governing word field.

source_jp:
あらざらむ
この世の外の
思ひ出に
今ひとたびの
逢ふこともがな
